question: Compare the top 3 open-source vector databases for a startup building RAG products
short_answer: Milvus is an open‑source, GPU‑accelerated vector database that can handle billions of vectors at lower cost but requires engineering resources. Weaviate provides a graph‑based vector store with a GraphQL API, modular design, hybrid search (vector + BM25 + metadata filters) and strong documentation. Qdrant is a budget‑conscious, Rust‑based vector database offering the best free tier, native sparse and multi‑vector model support, and excels at real‑time embedding search with rich JSON‑based payload filtering.

sources.title: Best Vector Databases in 2026: A Complete Comparison Guide
sources.snippet: Performance backs up the convenience. Tests show 7ms p99 latency, which means 99% of your queries return in under 7 milliseconds. Compare that to Elasticsearch's 1600ms for exact kNN in the same benchmark. The serverless tier auto-scales, so you don't provision capacity. You use what you need, pay for what you use. [...] The implementation uses HNSW indexing with scalar and binary quantization. Performance shows sub-50ms query latency at 15.3 million vectors (with quantization, 90-95% accuracy).
